script: Same bowl, just stretched. Gradient descent goes from one step to 284.
A round bowl. With the right step size, gradient descent lands on the bottom in one step.
Stretch it ten times along one direction. Even with its best step size, it now takes 29 steps, and it starts to zig-zag.
Stretch it a hundred times: 284 steps. It bounces between the steep walls, and crawls along the flat floor.

The curvatures across and along the valley are the Hessian's eigenvalues: one, and one hundredth. Their ratio is the condition number. The step has to suit the steepest direction, so along the floor it barely moves.
Momentum remembers its last step, and builds up speed along the floor: 23 steps.
Adam rescales each direction separately: 29 steps, on every one of these bowls, round or stretched.
Steepest over flattest curvature: the condition number. The bigger it is, the more plain gradient descent zig-zags.
